results.title: Private Ambulance Service (PAS) 2027
results.description:
East Midlands Ambulance Service NHS Trust (“EMAS”) is issuing this invitation to tender (ITT) under the provider selection regime (PSR), competitive process for the provision of Private Ambulance services where needed.

The intention is to award as separate lots and providers may bid for one or more of the lots if they are able to provide the necessary service within that area. This tender is based upon additional resource to EMAS using double crewed ambulance under blue light with a mix of Paramedic, Technicians and Emergency Care Assistants (ECA).

There is a total of 4 lots associated with this procurement as follow:
Lot 1 - South Lincolnshire
Lot 2 - Leicestershire
Lot 3 - Nottinghamshire and Derbyshire
Lot 4 - Northamptonshire

Providers must be CQC registered and hold all relevant licences required for carrying out this work.

The contract is for a 12 month period commencing on 1st April 2027 with an option to extend 12 months.

This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) Contract Notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 or the Procurement Act 2024 do not apply to this award.
results.buyer: East Midlands Ambulance Service NHS Trust

results.description:

results.title: Albert Cross Design Contest
results.description:
Glasgow City Council (GCC) is initiating a landmark architectural design contest to redevelop two prominent gap sites at Albert Cross, situated within the historic East Pollokshields Conservation Area. These sites were formerly occupied by B-listed tenement blocks, which were tragically lost to fires in 2019 and 2020.
The Design Contest is a call for architects to submit design proposals for both sites as part shared vision for the cross.  The contest will be run as a 2 stage process, commencing with the submission of an initial diagrammatic conceptual design which will be judged anonymously by the judging panel.  From this a shortlist of 3 entrants will be invited to develop their ideas further to the Stage 2 submission with Cost Plan and named design team, from which an outright winner will then be selected.
The depth and complexity of the Stage 2 submission information included should be in line with RIBA Plan of Work 2020 for an “early” Stage 3: Spatial Coordination (or for an “advanced” Stage 2: Concept Design)
It is envisaged that, subject to approvals and acquisition of the sites, the winner may be awarded a Design Services Contract to further their design proposal into a full planning application for one or both sites, at Council’s sole discretion.
More detailed information is contained within the Albert Cross Design Contest Brief which is available on the Public Contract Scotland Tendering Portal.
The Council accordingly reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to award a Design Services Contract for the further development of the winning design in accordance with the negotiated procedure without prior publication of a Contract notice in accordance with Regulation 33(6) of The Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.

results.title: The Provision of Tier 3 Community Dermatology Service on behalf of NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board
results.description:
This is a Community Tier 3 Dermatology Service.
This service aims to address the specific healthcare needs of patients who require access to dermatology services where the service is delivered across the Greater Manchester conurbation.
The Specification contains the requirements to ensure the delivery of a local, effective, integrated patient centred, community-based, dermatology service that gives timely advice, assessment, diagnosis and treatment. This is to be delivered in line with the GM strategic aim to deliver increased quality of care closer to patient's' homes.
The Contract to be awarded as a result of this Procurement will have an initial term of three years commencing from the Commencement Date (as defined in the Contract) which is expected to be on 1 April 2027. The Authority may extend the initial term of the Contract by a further period of two years to a maximum term of five years.
The indicative overall contract value is £26,975,375.25 for the initial three-year contract term and £17,983,583.50 for the optional two-year extension period, with an estimated annual value of £8,991,791.75 and an anticipated maximum total value of £44,958,958.75 including extensions.
For full details of the Service and any additional information regarding this Procurement please see link to the Specification and Invitation to Tender documentation that can be accessed via SAP Ariba.
Invitation to Tender documentation can be accessed via SAP Ariba reference Doc3193557990 at the link available in section I.III

results.title: CAWT PEACEPLUS Community Connections and Wellbeing project (CCWP) - Delivery of Psychosocial Activities and Community Supports (WHSCT & SHSCT Areas)
results.description:
Rooted in local communities and working with and through existing organisations and initiatives, the CAWT Community Connection and Wellbeing Project (CCWP) will strengthen capacity to improve health and wellbeing in participating communities.
The project aims to help people gain the skills, tools, knowledge, and confidence needed to enable them to harness new opportunities and access high-quality, accessible health and social care supports.
This procurement exercise and the subsequent service to be commissioned will cover only the Northern Ireland delivery Lot Areas, which are located within the boundaries of the Southern Health and Social Care Trust (SHSCT) and the Western Health and Social Care Trust (WHSCT).
The service will involve the delivery of psychosocial activities (1:1 and/or group-based) and community supports (1:1 and/or group-based).
Please refer to the full suite of tender documents for further information on the service requirements.

results.title: Reopening of the Over 65 Residential Care Home Framework for Swindon
results.description:
Swindon Borough Council invites expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced service providers for admission to the existing Over 65 Years of Age Residential Care Home Framework for Swindon.
Project Description
Swindon Borough Council is undertaking the first annual re-opening of its existing Residential Care Home Framework for adults aged 65 years and over within the Swindon locality. This Framework was originally commissioned under public contract regulations and will continue to use this until the end of the total term. This framework commenced on 1st January 2026 and is currently operating within the initial contract period. Existing Framework providers are not required to reapply as part of this process. Successful applicants will join the existing Framework from 1st January 2027.
This procurement exercise does not constitute a new procurement or re-tender of the Framework. It provides an opportunity for providers that are not currently admitted to the Framework, or that were unsuccessful in previous application rounds, to apply for admission to the Framework.
The Framework has an initial term ending on 31st December 2027, with the option for the Council to extend by up to two further periods of two years each, resulting in a maximum potential Framework duration of six years from the original commencement date. Providers admitted through this re-opening exercise may remain on the Framework for the remainder of the Framework term, subject to extension options being exercised and continued compliance with contractual requirements.
The estimated value of placements commissioned through the Framework during the period 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2027 is approximately £12 million, with a potential maximum Framework value of approximately £60 million should all extension periods be exercised.
The Framework will continue to be re-opened annually via the Supplying the South West Portal to allow additional providers to apply for admission.
The Framework will be advertised and all applicants must meet the minimum selection and award criteria to be admitted to the Framework.
This Framework is for in-borough residential care homes only.
For all over-65 residential care needs (standard, enhanced and complex), providers will be required to operate within the Council's published fee structure. Acceptance of the Council's fee structure will form part of the Framework requirements.
To participate, suppliers must register as a supplier with ProContract at www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk and register an interest in the opportunity before obtaining access to the tender documents. In the event of difficulties registering as a supplier, please contact the Proactis Support Team at ProContractSuppliers@proactis.com
Tender clarification deadline: 7th October 2026, 12:00 noon (UK Local Time). Clarification questions must be submitted via the Messaging facility within the ProContract portal. Responses will be issued periodically through the portal.
Tender submission deadline: 14th October 2026, 12:00 noon (UK Local Time), via the ProContract portal: https://www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk/
Please note that this opportunity may be advertised on Find a Tender Service, Contracts Finder and other procurement websites; however, Supplying the South West Portal is the only portal containing all documentation required to submit a response. The procurement reference is DN831353
No tender submissions will be considered without completing the tender documents in full, including all required attachments, and submitting them in accordance with the instructions contained within the tender documentation
